items.title: Somalia braces for El Niño floods as millions face risk of hunger
items.description: In Bayahaaw village, on the outskirts of Jowhar in central Somalia, farmers face a difficult choice: plant crops and risk losing them to floodwaters or leave their fields bare and face potential hunger in the coming year. Nuh Adan, a farmer and community leader in Bayahaaw, said flooding caused by breached riverbanks could devastate local agriculture for months. "If the river breaks and the floods hit us, the effects will last until the next rainy season in March," Adan said. items.title: Somalia: Xawaadle Elders and Al-Shabaab Reportedly Reach Truce in Hiiraan
items.description: A 16-point joint statement circulated by Al-Shabaab-affiliated media  said the sides had resolved their disputes and agreed to maintain peace in areas controlled or influenced by the clan. The reported agreement includes a commitment by Hawadle elders not to allow the recruitment or operation of Macawiisley fighters in their areas or provide them with shelter. Macawiisley forces from Hiiraan have played a key role in supporting Somali government troops against Al-Shabaab. The meeting in Maxaas was attended by dozens of traditional elders, while Al-Shabaab was represented by senior figures

items.title: Somali Clans sign peace agreement to end long-running conflict in Galmudug
items.description: Prime Minister Hamza Abdi Barre attended the ceremony, where traditional leaders Ugaas Mohamed Ugaas Kayse and Ugaas Hassan Ugaas Mohamed Ugaas Nuur signed the agreement. items.title: Journalists face arrests and alleged assaults while covering evictions in Somalia and Somaliland
items.description: The Somali Journalists Syndicate (SJS) says it has documented 13 arbitrary arrests of journalists in Mogadishu since Jan. 1, 2026, while 10 journalists have been arrested in Somaliland during the same period. Many of the cases involved reporters covering protests, forced evictions or criticism of government officials. items.title: Somalia: Heavy Fighting Erupts in Baidoa as Rival Forces Trade Claims
items.description: Residents reported hearing a series of powerful explosions across Baidoa, with thick plumes of smoke visible over parts of the city. Initial reports indicated that several locations, including a power facility and a base used by federal government forces, were struck during the clashes. Ugaas Hassan, the information minister for the Laftagareen-aligned faction, confirmed that its forces had launched an attack, describing the assault as involving several successive waves.   New footage, moment when Laftagaren's militias attacked #Baidoa this morning, one resident recorded. pic.twitter.com/

items.title: New Chapter, Same Stalemate: Somalia’s War with Al-Shabaab
items.description: The Somali government’s battle with Al-Shabaab militants grinds on, with neither able to gain a decisive advantage. To improve its lot, Mogadishu needs to bolster its military and alleviate civilian suffering in areas under insurgent control, while looking for openings for dialogue with the group.

items.title: Death toll rises to 139 after migrant boat capsizes off Djibouti
items.description: The boat went down during the night of Oct. 8-9 near Guehere, north of the port town of Obock. The death toll rose from 109 after 30 more bodies were recovered, the International Organization for Migration said. About 82 people survived, while search and recovery operations continued. The shipwreck is among the deadliest recorded on the Eastern Route, a migration corridor used by people traveling from the Horn of Africa toward Yemen and other destinations in the Arabian Peninsula. items.titleIt: Death toll rises to 139 after migrant boat capsizes off Djibouti
